in_text_mentions: In crusted scabies, thick hyperkeratotic crusts occur on the skin with erythroderma (Figures 4 and 5). This clinical picture can resemble psoriasis.17 The crusts carry millions of these mites and may shed them off to the patient’s environment, thereby infecting others. Unlike in classic scabies, in crusted scabies, a skin biopsy is almost always diagnostic as mites and ova can be easily visualised in the thickened stratum corneum (Figure 6). Peripheral eosinophilia and immunoglobulin E levels are usually raised in patients with crusted scabies.8,10,18

panels.rationale: Human H&E-stained penile skin biopsy from a patient diagnosed with crusted scabies. The section demonstrates mites and eggs in multiple stratum-corneum burrows, a specific diagnostic manifestation of the configured disease. [raw subtype: crusted scabies]

panels.figure_caption: Skin biopsy from glans showed hyperkeratosis, acanthosis of stratum malpighii. Stratum corneum revealed multiple subcorneal burrows containing Sarcoptes scabiei larvae and eggs. Dermis had inflammatory cell infiltration rich in eosinophils and lymphocytes (Hematoxylin & eosin stain, original magnification, ×20).
